data.summary: The 16‑week plan builds a solid foundation in the student’s weak Units 1 and 2 early, then cycles through the remaining units while revisiting earlier concepts. Each week uses the full 4 hours for focused study, live‑class integration, and timed practice, ending with two weeks of mixed review and exam‑style drills.

weeks.focus: Unit 1 foundations – moles, molar mass, and mass spectroscopy
tasks: Read the textbook sections for 1.1 and 1.2 and take concise notes.
Complete 15 practice problems on mole conversions and molar mass calculations.
Do 10 free‑response questions on mass spectroscopy, then compare answers to the scoring guide.
Watch a short video on elemental composition of pure substances.
Solve 12 problems on percent composition and empirical formulas.
Analyze 5 sample mixture problems and write balanced composition equations.

weeks.focus: Unit 1 – atomic structure and electron configuration
tasks: Create a chart of electron configurations for the first 20 elements.
Complete 8 photoelectron spectroscopy interpretation questions.
Do a timed set of 5 FRQs on electron configuration and PES.

weeks.focus: Unit 1 – periodic trends and valence electrons
tasks: Summarize periodic trends in a one‑page cheat sheet.
Work through 10 problems on ionic compound formation and valence electron counting.
Review 5 past FRQs that involve periodic trends and ionic compounds.

weeks.focus: Live class reinforcement for Unit 1 topics 1.1‑1.3
tasks: Attend live class #9300 and take detailed notes.
After class, redo the 15 mole‑conversion problems from Week 1 without notes.
Complete 8 additional FRQs on composition of mixtures, marking against the guide.

weeks.focus: Unit 2 – chemical bonds and intramolecular forces
tasks: Read textbook sections on 2.1 and 2.2 and draw bond‑type diagrams.
Solve 12 problems comparing covalent, ionic, and metallic bonding energies.
Write short explanations (2‑3 sentences) for 5 intramolecular potential energy curves.

weeks.focus: Unit 2 – structures of solids and metals
tasks: Create flashcards for crystal lattice types and metallic alloy structures.
Complete 10 lattice‑energy calculation problems.
Do 5 FRQs on properties of ionic solids and metallic bonding.

weeks.focus: Live class for Unit 2 Lewis diagrams and resonance
tasks: Attend live class #9301 and actively participate in the Lewis diagram exercises.
After class, draw Lewis structures for 8 given molecules, including formal charge calculations.
Complete 6 resonance‑structure FRQs and check answers with the scoring rubric.
Review VSEPR theory and make a table of shapes vs. steric number.
Solve 12 hybridization problems (sp, sp2, sp3).
Do 5 timed FRQs that require predicting molecular geometry.

weeks.focus: Unit 3 – intermolecular forces and properties of solids
tasks: Write a one‑page summary of IMFs and how they affect solid properties.
Complete 10 problems on boiling points, melting points, and lattice energies.
Answer 4 FRQs linking IMFs to solid-state properties.

weeks.focus: Unit 3 – phases and kinetic molecular theory
tasks: Derive the Ideal Gas Law from kinetic theory in a notebook.
Solve 12 gas‑law problems involving combined gas equations.
Do 6 FRQs that require applying KMT to explain phase changes.
Create a flowchart for writing net ionic equations.
Complete 10 stoichiometry word problems with limiting‑reactant calculations.
Practice 5 FRQs on reaction classification and stoichiometric balancing.

weeks.focus: Unit 5 – reaction rates and rate laws
tasks: Watch a tutorial on deriving rate laws from experimental data.
Solve 12 problems determining rate constants and reaction orders.
Do 5 FRQs that ask for writing and interpreting rate laws.
Create a table of enthalpy changes for common reactions.
Complete 10 calorimetry calculations (q = mcΔT).
Answer 4 FRQs on energy diagrams and heat transfer.
Do a 40‑minute timed practice set covering 20 FRQs from Units 1‑4.
Review each incorrect answer using the scoring guide and rewrite the solution.
Create a one‑page concept map linking atomic structure, bonding, and reaction stoichiometry.

weeks.focus: Comprehensive timed practice and exam strategy
tasks: Take a full‑length 90‑minute AP Chemistry practice exam (selected sections).
Score the exam, note weak areas, and write a 5‑minute reflection on test‑taking strategies.
Do a final 20‑minute review of any remaining trouble spots using flashcards.

data.final_week_advice: In the last week, simulate real exam conditions, focus on pacing, and use your reflection to fine‑tune strategies. Trust the foundations you built in Units 1 and 2, and stay calm—your consistent practice will pay off.
